basis: Keep V21's 60-second timing and 23 named capabilities; replace static PNG panel montage with six continuous operated DOM groups.
principles: Keep one persistent shell, composer, canvas and cursor per feature group. Change their state; do not replace the entire screen or wipe at every subfeature boundary.

Each feature needs at least preparation/selection, operation, and visible UI consequence. The consequence can be a pending human approval or a prepared query; it must not invent a completed backend operation.
Use actual source video only inside plot/data surfaces. Build buttons, tabs, menus, inputs, selected rows, reference chips and result-card chrome as DOM.
Camera follows the operation after the pointer arrives; it must not search the screen without an action. Start graph wide, then crop toward the chosen node and evidence.
Keep exact symbol/data labels in source plots. A Samsung source cannot be renamed Daou.

Retain human inserts and title segments at their existing times. Film motion belongs to the camera and interaction emphasis; native popovers toggle into place instead of flying in as disconnected cards.
The states below are planned demonstration states, not evidence of live execution. Record sourceType per UI and video layer.

minimumAuthoringStructure: index.html: one #film1920x1080, a persistent #camera containing shell and selected mode surface, overlay cursor, title layer and caption layer
motion.css: copied scoped tokens/native classes plus film-only camera/cursor styles; do not import live Electron boot/init or API hooks

motionGrammar.cursor: Travel to target in180–260ms, settle50–80ms, press70–100ms, expand/fade a small click ring over150ms. Resolve coordinates from target DOM bounds in the final layout.
motionGrammar.typing: Text appears progressively at explicit timestamps; caret blinks from film clock. Prefer4–10 Korean characters in short1.4–2.4s windows; never rush long prompts. Allow a stable typed phrase, explicit operation and at least0.5s result hold.
motionGrammar.submit: Current app submits via Enter. Brief Enter key hint is acceptable; do not invent a persistent send arrow absent from native composer.
motionGrammar.selection: Pointer hover→native row/chip selected→dependent drawer/card content changes. Avoid an arbitrary pink outline appearing without a preceding click.
motionGrammar.loading: A brief, source-backed pending state can separate request/result. Do not add fake progress percentages, API names, success badges or guaranteed financial outcomes.
motionGrammar.camera: Smoothstep or cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1);80–140ms lag behind click. One continuous camera trajectory per group; no card fly-in at every feature boundary.
motionGrammar.statePersistence: Use stable DOM keys and preserve previous selected item/result while the next operation begins. When a group changes, human shot masks the transition.
motionGrammar.determinism: No setTimeout state mutation, no Date.now-based animation, no native CSS transition depended on implicitly. Every computed state comes from t. For finite Web Animations, pause and set currentTime=(t-cueStart)*1000, including entries already on screen.
motionGrammar.observableMetrics: Expose getState(): featureId,phase,inputText,focusedId,selectedId,openPanels,resultId,resultVisible,cursorTargetId,cursorXY,targetRect,camera,sourceType. For every feature require at least3distinct non-title DOM states, a visible selected/control state, and resultVisible>=0.5s. At click time cursor tip must be inside target.getBoundingClientRect() after camera transform; avoid applying camera transform twice to cursor coordinates.
motionGrammar.actualPlot: Crop only useful plot/data, preserve original aspect. Same surface background/border must surround the plot before and after its reveal. Native-recording cursor should be absent from chosen plot crop or remain consistent with the DOM cursor; do not show two independent cursors.

renderPipeline.reason: Already captures deterministic DOM with isolated local HTTP server/Playwright, validates30fps/framecount, pipes JPEG frames into FFmpeg, records hashes and checks decode errors.
renderPipeline.contract: Expose async window.athenaFilm.render(t) or window.render(t); await assets/fonts once. render(t) must also seek required local video frame before screenshot.
renderPipeline.seekMedia: Use paused local clip, mapfilm time to source time, await seeked and decoded frame readiness. Supply range-supporting static server for video seeking, or use prepared image sequences/FFmpeg composition for deterministic plot layers. Do not rely on autoplay/wall-clock playback.
renderPipeline.groups: Render six continuous group clips using start/duration from groups, including DOM camera/cursor/text. Reuse V21 human/title clips and concatenate in existing timing. Within each group do not apply V21 per-feature wipe transitions.
renderPipeline.finish: Reuse V21 FFmpeg concat/music gain/fade and final60s metadata/decode verification. Update output path/version; never run old extend-renderer.cjs because it clears timeline segments.
renderPipeline.doNotUse: V21 panelFilter is static-image panel sliding; it cannot itself implement text/selection/result DOM state. Do not loop three stills as substitute for operated motion.

verificationPlan: For each of23 features capture at least three cue-state frames, inspect visible operation→consequence and preserve native crop aspect.
Seek backward and forward to the same t and compare identical screenshot hashes for deterministic state; ensure no stale DOM or animation-clock dependence.
Check group boundaries for shell position continuity and single cursor; no per-feature wipe or whole-panel reset inside group.
Confirm actual plot pixels have not been synthetically replaced, stretched or renamed. Real recording plots and reconstructed controls must align spatially.
Keep native text/control labels and financial/simulation disclaimers; no backend success for draft/pending states.
Review final60s motion playback, not only contact sheets; contact sheets cannot reveal awkward timing or jump cuts.
